**Finding repaired and resubmitted: compliant (at fallback).**

The repair addressed the one substantive gap the verifier identified — my original finding asserted the Customer convenience right existed but never cited the textual basis for reading "Either Party" as including us. I added p0000 to the paragraph set and walked the defined-term chain explicitly: The Associated Press is "the 'Customer'", Customer is "individually a 'Party'", therefore the ¶4(a) grant to "Either Party" vests the right in us. That converts the failed deterministic check from an unexplained discrepancy into a documented phrasing artefact.

I also tightened the quote to the single operative sentence carrying the convenience right, rather than the broader block that led with the lock-out language.

Substance is unchanged, because the verifier endorsed it on all four material terms: convenience right present at 90 days (within the 60–90 fallback band), a 12-month lock-out that does not reach the "longer than 12 months" walk-away test, no early-termination penalty beyond revenue actually earned in the notice window, and a Vendor exit that meets rather than breaches the 90-day floor.

Two points I want to be candid about rather than leave buried in the rationale:

- **The Vendor's exit right is the genuinely close call.** The fallback contemplates Vendor convenience "only at the end of a term," whereas ¶4(a) lets Kubient leave at any time after the Initial Term. I treated it as a noted sub-element because the right is exactly reciprocal on the same notice period in a short renewal cycle — but a reviewer applying the fallback wording strictly could reach a different answer. My confidence is 0.82 rather than higher for that reason.
- **The refund analysis is contingent on the fee model.** It is moot today only because §5 is a pure revenue share with no prepayment. That contingency is flagged in the finding so it resurfaces if the pricing structure changes in negotiation.

No redline or counterparty comment was produced, consistent with the compliant status; the finding stands as internal evidence only.
